old: This word names a quality by tacking a noun-making ending onto a word that already described something surrounding you.
It's formed from a word meaning 'surrounding' plus a suffix that turns qualities into nouns.
Think of its adjective cousin, 'ambient' — this word is just that idea turned into a thing you can feel in a room.
clues: This noun names something you sense on walking into a restaurant or hotel lobby, rather than anything you can see or touch. English made it by adding a noun ending to an adjective.
It means the overall feel of a place, shaped by lighting, sound and decor; a touch more refined than plain atmosphere, and a favorite word of restaurant reviewers.
It was built directly from its closest relative, ambient, the adjective behind ambient music and ambient lighting.
reviewNote: Clue 1 was too abstract to guess (solver said brightness); now anchors it to a setting.
